title: How do we draw lines of one tenth, three tenths and four fifths?
description: Three lengths are drawn on number lines by cutting the unit into equal parts and counting parts from zero. The board uses ten parts for tenths and five parts for fifths, then lays the two lines side by side to check the fourth fifth.
teaching_notes: One idea: the bottom number says how many equal parts to cut the unit into, and the top number says how many parts to count from zero. Watch for students who swap the two numbers.

video_script.why: A learner draws a line of a given fraction length by cutting the unit into equal parts and counting parts.
video_script.substitution: the book's own lengths one tenth, three tenths and four fifths
video_script.anchor: a number line from 0 to 1 cut into equal parts
video_script.payoff_line: Draw one tenth and three tenths on ten parts, and four fifths on five parts

final_answer.value: 1/10 is the 1st mark of 10 parts, 3/10 is the 3rd mark of 10 parts, 4/5 is the 4th mark of 5 parts (the same point as 8/10)
final_answer.spoken: one tenth and three tenths on ten parts, four fifths on five parts

video_script.fraction_reading: one tenth, three tenths, four fifths, eight tenths
maths_rules: tenths: cut 0 to 1 into 10 equal parts
1/10 ends at the 1st mark, 3/10 ends at the 3rd mark
fifths: cut 0 to 1 into 5 equal parts; 4/5 ends at the 4th mark
check: 1 fifth = 2 tenths, so 4 x 2 = 8 tenths and 4/5 ends where 8/10 would
video_script.design: Two number lines from zero to one, one with ten parts and one with five. The same method as the solved example: cut into equal parts, then count from zero.
